transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-18
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Head of ML, Nebula), Tomás Alvarez (Platform Eng, Nebula), Sara Gibson (CTO, Nebula)
---
Summary: POC scoping focused on capacity sizing, reserved GPU vs hosted pricing, burst/fallback policies, and success criteria for a 6-week pilot. Customer emphasized strict p95 latency targets for their checkout and personalization APIs, and data residency/KMS needs. Redwood AE/SE outlined a recommended POC plan with reserved capacity + burst pool, a fall back to quantized lower-cost model variant, and benchmarks to validate tail latency under realistic traffic.
Topics: success criteria, benchmarks, reserved GPUs, burst strategy, fallback policies, telemetry, timeline, security (SSO/SAML, KMS), integration tasks.
----
[00:00] Maya: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining. we're going to scope the poc for nebula's inference for personalization. quick intros?
[00:16] Priya: hey, i'm priya, lead the ml team, mostly on model infra and serving. our main goal is to reduce latency on the rec call that feeds checkout personalization.
[00:28] Tomás: tomás here, platform eng, i'll own infra bits and network. we need to understand VPC setup and KMS for keys.
[00:37] Sara: sara, cto, i'll be high level but want to be sure we don't regress cost or availability.
[00:45] Maya: great. luca, do you want to kick off on capacity ideas?
[00:48] Luca: yea, thanks. so based on what priya shared in the pre-call notes, you're expecting about ~700 rps at peak for the personalization endpoint with avg prompt sizes around 400 tokens and 95th token p95 target under 300ms end-to-end post-inference. is that right?
[01:10] Priya: yes rough numbers. the 700 peak is bursty — 10 minute spikes then back down to 150 rps baseline.
[01:19] Maya: okay so two dimensions: steady baseline and short high-frequency spikes. typical redwood pattern is reserved capacity sized to baseline with a burst pool for spikes.
[01:29] [01:29] Tomás: what does reserved mean in practice? dedicated gpus, reserved vcpu? network rules?
[01:34] Maya: reserved is a dedicated GPU pool — you reserve x GPUs for the POC so you have predictable throughput and no noisy neighbor. for the spike we recommend a burst pool (shared GPUs or hosted) that can autoscale for short windows.
[01:49] Priya: our compliance team requires keys to stay in our KMS and logs retained for 180 days — can that be honored on reserved?
[01:57] Luca: yes, on Redwood Private we integrate with customer KMS and ship audit logs; for Dedicated we can also configure KMS binding and log forwarding. we'll add specifics in the security doc.
[02:08] [02:08] Sara: latency target again — 300ms p95 post-inference. what's realistic with reserved + burst?
[02:16] Luca: depends on model size and quantization. for a 3B dense model on a V100/RTX-class we typically see ~80-120ms per request inference if KV cache hits and short sequences; the tail depends on batching and network hop. our recommendation: run a 2-week benchmark with your traffic shape and measure p50/p95/p99.
[02:35] Priya: ok, can you explain the fallback policy you mentioned earlier?
[02:39] Maya: sure. fallback = if burst capacity exhausted or latencies exceed SLO, route to a lighter, quantized model variant (same family but 4-bit quant) or a smaller architecture. also can route to a hosted lower-tier model to preserve availability.
[02:52] Tomás: what about consistency — we can't have answers shifting wildly in checkout. how do you guard quality?
[02:59] Luca: good q. we do A/B tests and can pin rollout by route. for POC we'll run side-by-side evals for a sample of requests: compare embeddings or generation diffs and set accept/reject thresholds. also configurable canary traffic to watch human-facing metrics.
[03:15] [03:15] Priya: the product needs deterministic-ish responses. latencies >500ms will trigger customer complaints. fallback model latency must still be <250ms ideally.
[03:25] Maya: agreed. so success criteria suggestion: 95th latency <= 300ms for 95% of test windows, fallback correctness metric within 3% degradation vs baseline on our test eval set, and <0.5% error/availability incidents during POC.
[03:42] Sara: timeline? we want to be in a pilot in 6 weeks. is that feasible?
[03:47] Luca: yes — proposed plan: week 1: ingest traffic profile + share benchmark harness; week 2: allocate reserved pool + baseline run; weeks 3-4: stress tests with burst scenarios + fallback simulation; week 5: production-like run and metrics review; week 6: finalize handoff and runbook.
[04:06] [04:06] Tomás: do you need network peering or can we use internet egress? we prefer strict VPC peering for data controls.
[04:13] Maya: for Private/Dedicated we can set up VPC peering or private link. we'll capture network requirements on the follow-up.
[04:20] Priya: ok, on sizing — what numbers are you thinking for reserved GPUs?
[04:24] Luca: rough calc: 700 rps baseline? you said baseline 150 rps and 10-min 700 peaks. we size reserved to baseline plus 20% headroom so baseline 150 -> reserved capacity to handle ~180 rps steady. then burst handles the 700 spikes. for a 3B model on an A10-like GPU (approx), one GPU can do ~250-300 rps depending on batch, so 1 GPU may cover baseline. but for tail latency and concurrency we recommend 2 reserved GPUs for redundancy and headroom.
[04:55] Priya: 2 GPUs reserved + burst seems reasonable. burst pool cost — is that per-minute? how charged?
[05:03] Maya: burst is usage-based for the POC; we can show cost-per-token and per-gpu-hour. for dedicated reserved is a fixed monthly rate pro-rated for the POC term. we'll include exact cost numbers in the spreadsheet.
[05:17] [05:17] Tomás: how fast can burst scale? we need sub-60s scale up for those 10 minute spikes.
[05:22] Luca: autoscale can allocate additional nodes in under a minute for warm pools; cold provisioning from zero can take several minutes. our recommendation: keep a warm burst pool (small) and allow quick scale out to meet 10-minute spikes within 30-60s.
[05:37] Priya: if warm pool is always on, cost goes up. what's the tradeoff?
[05:41] Maya: tradeoff is cost vs availability. for POC we often keep a tiny warm pool (1-2 GPUs) and allow scaling to more; this blends predictability with lower cost.
[05:51] [05:51] Sara: telemetry — what do we need to ship so you can reproduce traffic shape?
[05:54] Luca: 7-day token histogram, per-request size distribution, example traces with timestamps, and a synthetic replay script will be enough. we'll provide the harness and step-by-step guide.
[06:06] Priya: ok, i can pull histograms. question on kv cache — do you support prefix caching for personalization? sometimes we have long histories per user.
[06:15] Luca: yes, we have KV cache and prefix caching. note transcription: K V cache sometimes transcribed differently in our notes — but it's the same. for personalization we recommend sharding keys and using local KV warmers for hot users.
[06:29] [06:29] Tomás: how do fallbacks interact with stateful sessions? if we switch to a quantized model mid-session, will the kv cache be invalid?
[06:36] Luca: good point. fallback with full session semantics is tricky. options: 1) keep a compatible quantized variant with shared cache format so KV is portable; 2) rebuild context on fallback which costs latency; 3) prefer stateless fallbacks for short requests. for the POC we'll test option 1 (compatible quant variant).
[06:53] Priya: we need to measure regression on personalization quality. can Redwood run a delta eval?
[06:58] Maya: yes, we'll run automated evals against your holdout and produce precision/recall or ranking delta. we'll define thresholds together.
[07:06] [07:06] Sara: any red flags from a reliability perspective?
[07:09] Luca: only usual: if bursts are huge and sustained, cost and tail latencies rise. also cross-region failover needs to be configured if you require multi-region availability.
[07:20] Tomás: cross-region we probably won't need for POC. single-region peering is fine.
[07:24] [07:24] Maya: let's talk about benchmarks — we'll run three scenarios: baseline steady-state, burst spike replay (10-minute spikes), and degraded mode where we simulate node loss and force fallback. each run will capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cold-start times.
[07:43] Priya: cold-starts are important — many of our spikes are after a lull so cold is realistic. can you capture cold vs warm latency breakdown?
[07:51] Luca: absolutely. we'll do warm, warm+cache, and cold starts. we'll instrument client-side and server-side traces.
[07:59] [07:59] Priya: what's the plan for model quantization — will we lose quality?
[08:03] Luca: quant tradeoffs depend on model. 4-bit quant often has negligible quality loss for many tasks but we need to validate on your dataset. for ranking/personalization small shifts can have outsized product impact, so we must measure.
[08:16] Maya: propose success criteria recap: p95 <= 300ms 95% windows, fallback quality delta < 3% on ranking metrics, and cost < X (we'll compute).
[08:27] [08:27] Tomás: on metrics collection — what dashboards do you provide?
[08:30] Luca: Redwood Console provides per-route token cost, latency heatmaps, token-level breakdown, and tracing hooks. we can grant Nebula a 30-day view for the pilot.
[08:41] Priya: will logs contain sensitive customer PII? we need to scrub before shipping.
[08:45] Maya: we can redact or not collect request bodies; for audit you'll get metadata only. for deeper debugging we'll use hashed or redacted samples with your approval.
[08:56] [08:56] Sara: procurement question — can we get a short-term reserved rate for 6 weeks?
[09:01] Maya: typically we pro-rate reserved capacity monthly — we can offer a 6-week pro-rated invoice. procurement/legal we'll loop in and share standard terms + SOC2.
[09:12] [09:12] Priya: demo-level ask: can we get a sample workload that emulates our 10-minute spikes?
[09:17] Luca: yes, we'll supply a replay tool with config to adjust rps, token length, and concurrency. you'll be able to run it from your env to our test endpoint or we can run it in our infra.
[09:29] Priya: run it in our env preferred to test peering.
[09:32] Maya: noted. we'll deliver the harness and docs.
[09:35] [09:35] Tomás: what sort of fallbacks for model size are available? you mentioned smaller arch; list please.
[09:40] Luca: recommended fallbacks: same-family quantized variant (e.g., 3B -> 3B-4bit), smaller dense model (3B -> 1.5B), or hosted micro model (0.5B) for critical low-latency paths. tradeoffs: quality vs latency/cost.
[09:58] Priya: can we have a rule engine to prefer fallback based on route + real-time latency?
[10:04] Maya: yes, Redwood routing policies can be per-route with rules like latency thresholds, capacity exhaustion, or percent-based fallback. we can configure automatic fallback when average CPU/GPU util > 85% or p95 > threshold.
[10:18] [10:18] Sara: ok let's talk numbers — if we reserve 2 GPUs and keep 1 warm burst, and allow scaling to 6 GPUs during spikes, what's the expected latency profile?
[10:28] Luca: roughly: reserved 2 GPUs handles baseline with p95 ~ 120-180ms depending on batching; warm burst adds capacity so first scale steps keep p95 < 300ms; full scale to 6 GPUs should bring p95 closer to baseline. cold scale from zero will add a 2-3s penalty for new nodes.
[10:45] Priya: we can't tolerate 2-3s at any point for checkout. so cold scale is a no-go unless it's hidden behind async flows.
[10:54] Maya: agreed. for checkout we should rely on warm burst and conservative reserved sizing to eliminate cold starts.
[11:02] [11:02] Tomás: on the instrumentation side we'll want spans that tie back to request ids. is there a tracing header you recommend?
[11:08] Luca: we support x-request-id; also integrate with OpenTelemetry if you want end-to-end traces. we'll share example trace instrumentation.
[11:17] Priya: internal question — are there restrictions on model quantization licenses? some models have license constraints.
[11:22] Maya: yes, model licensing matters. we curate open models and disclose license terms. if you want a specific model, we'll confirm license for quantization and serving.
[11:32] [11:32] Sara: can we do an offline benchmark run that we can include in procurement pack?
[11:36] Maya: yes, we can produce a benchmark report with graphs and cost tables you can include.
[11:43] Priya: for the diving into fallback correctness — how will you present diffs? token-level diff? ranking delta?
[11:50] Luca: we'll give both: n-gram diffs, embedding distances, and ranking metrics like NDCG/Precision@K for your tasks. also qualitative examples for human review.
[11:58] [11:58] Tomás: in the POC, who has root access to infra? we need clear boundaries.
[12:03] Maya: Redwood manages the serving fabric; you retain control over your keys and VPC. we'll define roles and RBAC for the project.
[12:11] Priya: ok. out of curiosity — any gotchas for KV cache eviction when autoscaling?
[12:17] Luca: eviction can cause partial cold behavior; best practice is sticky routing for hot users or replicate hot cache shards across nodes. for POC we'll instrument cache hit ratios.
[12:30] [12:30] Priya: let's define final success criteria again and sign off — we want concrete thresholds for pass/fail.
[12:36] Maya: i'll read one proposed set: 1) p95 <= 300ms for 95% of evaluation windows during baseline and burst replay; 2) fallback model quality delta < 3% on NDCG/Precision@10; 3) no more than one availability incident >1 minute; 4) cost estimate within +/- 15% of projection. agree?
[12:58] Sara: that seems fair.
[13:01] [13:01] Priya: what about observability — retention of detailed traces for 180 days was requested. is that doable?
[13:07] Luca: retention is an add-on but for POC we can enable 90 days; 180 may need procurement add-on. we'll note that as a potential cost.
[13:18] Maya: we'll call that out in the cost sheet.
[13:20] [13:20] Tomás: security call: we'll need SAML SSO for console access.
[13:25] Maya: we support SAML and SCIM provisioning. we'll share the SSO setup doc.
[13:32] Priya: ok timelines again — you mentioned sample harness by monday?
[13:36] Maya: we'll aim to share the harness and initial capacity spreadsheet by 2026-09-20. luca, is that okay?
[13:41] Luca: yes, i'll push the harness and a step-by-step README.
[13:45] [13:45] Priya: great. one more technical — during fallback to hosted model, how do you preserve user-specific personalization vectors?
[13:53] Luca: if vectors live in your vector store we can call out-of-band; otherwise we can pass hashed context. there is work to be done to make vector lookups seamless across variants. for POC we recommend keeping vectors in your store and call it from the client so both models can access the same context.
[14:13] Maya: good note. we'll include a recommended architecture diagram in the follow-up.
[14:19] [14:19] Priya: any other vendor comparisons worth noting? we mentioned openai and anthropic earlier.
[14:24] Maya: main difference is our dedicated + private runtimes and granular routing + fallback policies optimized for production economics. we'll include a short comparison sheet.
[14:36] Tomás: for the burst pricing — if we go over scale often what are options? move to larger reserved or negotiate committed burst credits?
[14:44] Maya: yes, options: increase reserved, add committed burst credits, or tune batching/quantization to lower per-token cost. we'll look at actual numbers after initial runs.
[14:55] [14:55] Priya: let's record the low-hanging integrations: SSO/SAML, VPC peering, KMS integration, sample harness + replay, and preliminary cost sheet.
[15:05] Maya: noted. those will be in the next email.
[15:09] [15:09] Sara: i might drop off shortly but happy with the plan.
[15:12] Maya: quick check — are there any absolute deal brakes?
[15:15] Priya: only if we can't keep PII out of logs or KMS can't be used.
[15:20] Luca: on KMS we can do customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private.
[15:25] [15:25] Priya: ok good.
[15:27] Maya: folks, we'll run a stress test scenario during week 3 that simulates your 10-minute spikes. expected deliverable: benchmark report + cost spreadsheet + runbook at end of week 5.
[15:39] Tomás: who will be the day-to-day project contact?
[15:42] Maya: maya for procurement and timeline, luca for technical. we'll cc a solutions eng tracker.
[15:49] [15:49] Priya: thanks. any other technical deep-dive items now?
[15:52] Luca: one more: graceful degradation patterns — do you want to degrade to cached results first or fallback model first?
[15:59] Priya: cached results first for personalization probably better than producing weaker generated answers.
[16:04] Maya: we'll set the fallback order: 1) cached result, 2) quantized same-family model, 3) smaller model, 4) hosted micro-model. that order can be tuned per route.
[16:18] [16:18] Tomás: fine. regarding alerts — we need integration with pagerduty.
[16:22] Maya: pagerduty hooks available. we'll add alert thresholds for p95 and error rates in the runbook.
[16:31] Priya: is there a postmortem cadence you recommend if incident occurs during POC?
[16:36] Luca: 72-hour postmortem and we can provide RCA with kernel traces if needed.
[16:41] [16:41] Sara: ok i'm comfortable. anything else on legal side?
[16:45] Maya: legal will send a brief MSA and SOC2. procurement will follow.
[16:51] [16:51] Priya: last question — can we pin model version for the pilot so production won't shift under us?
[16:56] Luca: yes, model pinning and versioned rollouts are supported. we'll include that in config examples.
[17:03] Maya: great. sounds like we have alignment. i'll summarize next steps in an email and attach the harness + spreadsheet early next week.
[17:12] [17:12] Tomás: thanks, appreciate it.
[17:14] Priya: thanks everyone.
[17:16] Sara: thanks.
[17:18] [17:18] (call ends)
---
Recap (auto-gen):
- Recommended reserved pool: 2 GPUs (redundancy + baseline headroom)
- Warm burst pool: 1-2 GPUs, autoscale up to 6 GPUs for spikes
- Fallback order: cache -> quantized variant -> smaller model -> hosted micro-model
- Success criteria: p95 <= 300ms, fallback quality delta < 3%, <=1 availability incident>1min, cost within +/-15%
- Deliverables: benchmark harness, capacity/cost spreadsheet, security/SAML/KMS docs, schedule for network deep-dive
